_provenance.what: The workspace industry setting each committed firm book is served UNDER — the third field of GET /api/period/{id} that decides whether the report's sector-calibrated content may render.
_provenance.why: Every saga_10_col_*.json carries `industry: null`, because capture.py captures `statements` from a book with no workspace attached. A null industry agrees with nothing and disagrees with nothing, so the disagreement path the owner actually met — a LIVE Agras report headed 'Real estate · residential rental' over 301/341/345/371 and 70.5M of cost of sales — was reachable by no committed artefact. This file is the missing join.
_provenance.how_to_compose: statements = saga_10_col_<book>.json .statements, with `industry` set to displays[<key>] and `industry_signal` set to industry_signal.json[<book>][<key>]. That is exactly how pipeline.py:7711 assembles the served payload: the display label off organizations.industry_display_name, the signal off engine.industry.build_industry_signal(line_items, industry_key=...).
_provenance.displays_are_not_keys: `statements.industry` is organizations.industry_display_name — a LABEL. The rule registry scopes on the KEY. Both are recorded here so a consumer never has to invent one from the other.
_provenance.regenerated_by: tests/engine/fixtures/firm/capture_industry_signal.py writes industry_signal.json for exactly these (book, key) pairs; tests/engine/test_structural_industry_signal.py reds if that goes stale. This file is the index over it and is checked by frontend/lib/__tests__/industryFixtureIsReal.test.ts.
